The harder you kick (force), and the smaller the area of your foot on contact (area), the faster the ball will go and create more pressure as its force is concentrated on a smaller space, similar to how sharp objects press harder.  Conversely, if you spread out your foot across a bigger area when kicking, the force is less concentrated, leading to slower speed of the ball and lower pressure.
analogies.cooking: Imagine you're spreading batter evenly across a large cookie sheet before putting it in an oven. The same amount of batter will spread thin and make a light layer on the pan, but if you put all that batter into a smaller space, like a muffin cup, the pressure will be much higher.  This is similar to how pressure works – more force concentrated on a smaller area leads to higher pressure.

subject: Physics
standard_explanation: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium into another because its speed changes at the boundary. Light slows down when it enters a denser medium such as water or glass and bends towards the normal, and it speeds up and bends away from the normal when it enters a less dense medium. This change of direction is why a straw standing in a glass of water appears bent or broken at the surface.

analogies.free: Imagine a swimmer crossing a river towards a shallower area.  They'll feel their speed change as they enter the shallow water, and their trajectory will shift slightly to continue on that path even though their starting point was different.
analogies.everyday: Imagine you're driving down a road with a slight incline, and your car accelerates on that slope.  This is similar to light as it passes from air into water; the speed of light changes when it encounters denser media, causing it to bend like the car accelerating up the hill. This bending happens because the density of the medium affects the speed at which light travels through it.
analogies.sports: Imagine a baseball pitcher throwing a curveball. The ball bends in a specific way due to its spin, right?  Similarly, light bending as it travels from air into water is like spinning a football so that it curves when entering a different medium, but unlike our hands-on sports, this change is caused by the varying speeds of light through different materials.
analogies.cooking: Imagine you're kneading dough for a cookie recipe. When you put flour and water together to make dough, they don't mix perfectly right away.  The dough moves differently in different areas of the bowl, causing some parts to get denser or less dense than others – just like light behaves differently when it travels through different mediums.

subject: Mathematics
standard_explanation: A logarithm answers the question of what power a fixed base must be raised to in order to produce a given number, so the logarithm of 1000 to base 10 is 3 because 10 raised to the power 3 equals 1000. Logarithms are the inverse operation of exponentiation and turn multiplication into addition, which lets them compress an enormous range of values into a manageable scale. This is why quantities such as pH, sound in decibels, and earthquake magnitude are measured on logarithmic scales.

analogies.free: Think of a dimmer switch.  The dimmer controls how much light shines through, just like a logarithm determines the power that a base must be raised to reach a specific number. The dimmer represents a logarithmic scale because you can adjust the intensity level (or "magnitude") by changing its position on the scale.
analogies.everyday: Think of a dimmer switch for your bedroom lights. The dimmer control, like logarithms, takes a big number (like the light brightness) and lets you find the power the bulb needs to be at to reach that specific level, from completely off to full bright.
analogies.sports: Imagine you're playing a team sport where scoring involves a complex system of power boosts. The "logarithm" is like understanding how much of that boost power you need to reach the target score on your own.  You need to know exactly what level of intensity (power) will allow you to achieve a specific goal.
analogies.cooking: Imagine a cake recipe where you need to know how much of each ingredient to use based on the desired size of the final product. A logarithm acts like a secret code that tells you exactly what power of an ingredient (like baking soda or flour) to add, allowing you to adjust the quantity accurately to get the desired outcome – just like adjusting the amount of sugar in a recipe changes its sweetness level!

subject: Chemistry
standard_explanation: In an exothermic reaction the products store less chemical energy than the reactants, so the surplus energy is released to the surroundings, usually as heat, and the surroundings become warmer. In an endothermic reaction the products store more energy than the reactants, so energy is absorbed from the surroundings and they become cooler. Burning a fuel is exothermic, whereas the reaction inside an instant cold pack is endothermic.

analogies.free: Imagine a balloon filled with helium. When you release the pin holding the balloon down, the helium inside quickly escapes (exothermic reaction), causing the balloon to deflate and lose its upward thrust (energy released). In contrast, when you put your hand under cold water in a cup, it feels colder because energy is being absorbed from your hand (endothermic reaction) into the water.
analogies.everyday: Imagine your fridge as a place where cold air is stored. When you open the door and take out a hot bottle of water from outside, the cold air inside the fridge absorbs some of that heat energy to keep things cool - like an endothermic reaction. But when you put in frozen food or cook something on the stovetop, your fridge releases that excess heat into the environment to maintain its temperature, similar to how exothermic reactions release energy as heat.
analogies.sports: Imagine a basketball game where the team scoring goals (products) gets more energy from the other team's efforts (reactants). The final score is higher for them and they release leftover energy as heat to the environment (surroundings), making the temperature of the area around them rise.  Now imagine a game with teams that need to take energy from the environment (like an ice pack) to stay cool, where the energy required to do so lowers their overall temperature.
analogies.cooking: Imagine you're making cookies.  Baking them requires energy input (endothermic reaction) because you're turning raw ingredients into something tasty, which takes heat to happen. Burning a candle, however, is like an exothermic reaction - it releases energy in the form of light and heat as the fuel burns away.

subject: Biology
standard_explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy, captured by the pigment chlorophyll, to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. The captured light energy is stored as chemical energy in the bonds of the glucose, which the plant later uses for growth and respiration. It is effectively the reverse of respiration and is the ultimate source of almost all food and oxygen on Earth.

analogies.free: Photosynthesis is like a plant's kitchen, where sunlight acts as the stovetop, chlorophyll is the chef mixing ingredients, carbon dioxide is the flour and water the yeast, all creating glucose (the delicious meal) that fuels the plant's growth and provides oxygen for us to breathe.
analogies.everyday: Imagine a plant as a tiny factory that uses sunlight like an energy source to turn water and carbon dioxide into the fuel (glucose) it needs for growth, just like your mom cooks ingredients in the oven to create dinner from raw materials.  This process releases oxygen, which is like air freshener for our planet, allowing us to breathe.
analogies.sports: Photosynthesis is like a team of athletes training for a big game – the plants use sunlight as their energy source, just like they get from the coach's instructions (chlorophyll), to transform carbon dioxide and water into a high-energy meal (glucose) – the food that helps them grow strong. Just like a team needs oxygen to breathe and perform, plants also need to release oxygen after producing glucose during photosynthesis.
analogies.cooking: Imagine a kitchen where sunlight is like a powerful oven, and plants are the chefs. They use the light energy from the sun to mix carbon dioxide (like flour) and water (like yeast) into glucose (like dough), creating delicious sugars that fuel their growth. This process also releases oxygen as a byproduct, which we can then breathe!
